detailed_description: The Barcode Generator creates a live SVG preview of a linear barcode directly in the browser. Enter the value, choose Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, or UPC-A, and the preview updates using the rules of the selected symbology. For EAN-13 and UPC-A, use numeric values with the expected length; if the value does not fit the selected format, the page shows an error instead of rendering an invalid barcode. The tool is useful for quick test codes, mock label layouts, and checking how a short value looks in common barcode formats. It is intended for browser preview only, without image-file export, print-resolution controls, styling controls, or print-grade label validation.
usage_steps: Choose a barcode format: Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, or UPC-A.
Enter the text or numeric value in the content field.
For EAN-13 or UPC-A, make sure the value matches the numeric requirements for that format.
Review the SVG barcode preview on the page.
If an error appears, adjust the value or choose another barcode format.
Change the value or format again whenever you need a new preview.
usage_examples: Preview an internal inventory code in Code 128 before placing it in a mock label.
Check how a sample EAN-13 value renders for a product card draft.
Compare Code 39 and Code 128 for a short warehouse test label.
Validate a demo UPC-A value before using it in a presentation mockup.

faqs.question: Which barcode types are supported?
faqs.answer: The current interface supports Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, and UPC-A.

faqs.question: Why does EAN-13 or UPC-A show an error?
faqs.answer: Those formats require a valid numeric value. If the input does not match the selected format, the generator shows an error instead of an incorrect barcode.

faqs.question: Can I download the barcode as an image file?
faqs.answer: No. The current page shows an SVG preview in the browser, but it does not include a separate image download button.

faqs.question: Is this enough for final product labels?
faqs.answer: Use it for quick checks and mockups. For production labels, verify scanner requirements, size, contrast, and the relevant labeling standard.
